rules.title: Single country rule set DE
rules.statement: All parameters (minimum grade, benefit %, commute %, mileage rate) come from the one fleet_rule row with country 'DE': min_grade 6, benefit_pct 1.00, commute_pct 0.030, mileage_rate 0.305 EUR/km.
rules.note: Country is a literal; fleet_rule.currency is never read, EUR is hard-coded in the pages.

rules.title: Requester must exist and be active
rules.statement: A car request is only accepted for an employee whose number (trimmed, upper-cased) exists and whose status is 'A'; any other status (e.g. 'T') is refused.
rules.note: leave_date and hire_date are not checked; only status decides. See JP-R31 for the statement side.

rules.title: Grade threshold for a company car
rules.statement: An employee is entitled to a company car only if grade (Entgeltgruppe) >= fleet_rule.min_grade (DE: 6); grades 1-5 are refused.

rules.title: One open car per employee
rules.statement: An employee who already has an open assignment (end_date null) cannot request another car.

rules.title: Pool car availability
rules.statement: A pool car is offered only if it has no owner AND no open assignment; the list is sorted by plate and is computed once when step 1 passes.
rules.evidence: v.owner is null and not exists ... (select a from Assignment a where a.vehicle = v and a.endDate is null) order by v.plate

rules.title: Pool choice requires a selected car
rules.statement: When 'pool' is chosen (the default), a vehicle must be selected before step 3.

rules.title: New car mandatory data
rules.statement: When registering a newly delivered car, plate, make, model, list price (EUR) and CO2 (g/km) are all mandatory; fuel defaults to Diesel 'D' (choices D/P/H/E). No range check on price or CO2.
rules.evidence: plate == null || make == null || model == null || listPrice == null || co2 == null
rules.note: Negative or zero list price is accepted by the code; plate uniqueness is only the DB UNIQUE constraint (insert fails).

rules.title: Plate normalisation on entry
rules.statement: A new car plate is trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed to one space and upper-cased; blank becomes missing.

rules.title: Handover date default and no checks
rules.statement: The handover (start) date defaults to today, entered as dd.MM.yyyy, with no check against past/future or previous assignments.

rules.title: Request is delivered immediately
rules.statement: Submitting the wizard in one transaction: stores a new car (registered_on = handover date) or reuses the pool car, sets the car's owner to the employee, records a car_request with status 'DELIVERED' and requested_on = today, and opens an assignment starting on the handover date with no end date.
rules.note: The page is called 'Antrag' (request) but there is no approval or ordering state: status is always DELIVERED and the car is assigned at once.

rules.title: No re-check at submit (pool race)
rules.statement: The pool car chosen in step 2 is not re-checked for availability at submit, so two concurrent wizards can assign the same pool car.
rules.note: No DB constraint prevents two open assignments for one vehicle; the business intent (one holder per car) is only enforced at step-1 listing time.

rules.title: Owner mirrors open assignment
rules.statement: A car's owner is set when an assignment opens and cleared when it is returned; owner is meant to equal the holder of the open assignment.

rules.title: Return lookup by exact plate
rules.statement: A return is found by exact, case-sensitive plate match (no normalisation) and must have an open assignment, otherwise an error is shown.
rules.evidence: where v.plate = :p ... where a.vehicle = :v and a.endDate is null
rules.note: Wizard normalises plates on entry but return does not, so 'm-ab 1234' finds nothing.

rules.title: Odometer mandatory on return
rules.statement: A return requires an odometer reading (km); no range or plausibility check against earlier readings.

rules.title: Return date not before handover
rules.statement: Return date (default today) must not be before the assignment start date; same-day return and future dates are allowed.

rules.title: Booking a return
rules.statement: Booking a return sets assignment.end_date = return date, clears the car's owner (back to pool) and stores a car_return with return date, odometer km and condition note, in one transaction.

rules.title: Mileage amount
rules.statement: Business-trip reimbursement = km x fleet_rule.mileage_rate (DE 0.305 EUR/km), rounded to 2 decimals HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding); the amount is frozen on the claim at submission.
rules.note: Benefit uses HALF_UP; mileage uses HALF_EVEN. E.g. 1 km=0.305->0.30 (HALF_EVEN), would be 0.31 HALF_UP. Seed: 130 km -> 39.65.

rules.title: Mileage claim km must be positive
rules.statement: A claim is accepted only with km > 0 (integer kilometres); no upper limit; preview (Berechnen) computes for any km including <= 0.

rules.title: New claims start SUBMITTED
rules.statement: A new claim is stored with status 'SUBMITTED', claim date default today (no date check), purpose defaulting to empty text.

rules.title: Claim history window
rules.statement: The mileage page lists the employee's claims with claim_date between now minus 6 months and now, oldest first, all statuses.
rules.evidence: from.add(Calendar.MONTH, -6); claims = fleet.claims(employee, from.getTime(), new Date());
rules.note: Bounds carry the current time of day, so a claim dated exactly 6 months ago is likely excluded (DATE vs timestamp).

rules.title: Statement default period
rules.statement: The benefit statement period is given as yyyy-MM; if empty it defaults to the previous calendar month (server clock); it covers day 1 to the last day of that month.
rules.note: SimpleDateFormat is lenient: '2026-13' becomes January 2027; unparseable text throws.

rules.title: Benefit days per assignment
rules.statement: For each assignment overlapping the month, benefit days = inclusive days from max(start, 1st) to min(end or month-end, month-end); assignments not overlapping are skipped. Both the return day and a same-day new start count.

rules.title: Monthly benefit formula (1% + 0.03%/km)
rules.statement: Monthly benefit = list price x benefit_pct/100 + list price x commute_pct/100 x commute_km (DE: 1% + 0.03% per one-way commute km), unrounded.
rules.note: Uses current vehicle list price and current employee commute_km, not values at that time. CO2/fuel (EV reductions) ignored. No employee contribution and no per-vehicle %, unlike FLEBEN01 (VH-BPCT/1200 - EM-CNTRB).

rules.title: Benefit proration and rounding
rules.statement: Line benefit = monthly benefit x days / days in month, rounded to 2 decimals HALF_UP; total benefit = sum of rounded lines (EUR).
rules.note: Page states the monthly 1% rule but code prorates by calendar days; the German 1% rule normally charges a full month for any started month. E.g. 40000 EUR, 20 km, 15 of 30 days: (400+240)x15/30 = 320.00.

rules.title: Statement mileage counts approved only
rules.statement: Reimbursed business-trip total = sum of amounts of claims dated in the month with status 'APPROVED'; SUBMITTED and REJECTED are excluded.
rules.note: The portal only ever writes SUBMITTED and has no approval step, so portal-entered claims never reach this total; seed has APPROVED rows set outside the app.

rules.title: Statement not restricted to active employees
rules.statement: The statement is computed for any employee number found (exact match, no trim/upper-case), including status 'T'.

rules.title: No closed periods
rules.statement: Statements are computed on every view and never stored; there is no period open/close, so later changes (list price, commute km, returns) recompute past months.

rules.title: Current car is first open assignment
rules.statement: The employee's current car is the first assignment without end date in start-date-descending order; history shows all assignments incl. returned.
rules.evidence: if (a.isOpen()) { return a; ... order by a.startDate desc

rules.title: Employee search
rules.statement: Search is a case-insensitive contains match on employee number, last name or first name, sorted by last then first name, at most 50 rows, showing each one's current car plate; empty term lists the first 50.
rules.evidence: lower(e.employeeNo) like :t ... or lower(e.lastName) like :t or lower(e.firstName) like :t order by e.lastName, e.firstName ... setMaxResults(50)

rules.title: Wizard back skips validation
rules.statement: 'Zurueck' goes back one step (not below 1) without validating input.

rules.title: Statement days not capped at leaving date
rules.statement: Statement benefit days are the overlap of the assignment (start, end or month-end) with the calendar month only; employee.leave_date and hire_date are never read, so a leaver's open or late-closed assignment is taxed to the end of the month, and there is no leaver flag on the statement.
rules.evidence: Date e = a.getEndDate() == null || a.getEndDate().after(to) ? to : a.getEndDate();
rules.note: getHireDate()/getLeaveDate() have no caller in src/ (grep). Counterpart of MF-R35/MF-R40 (FLEBEN01 caps car days at EM-LEAV and flags L).

rules.title: Mileage claim accepted for any found employee
rules.statement: Mileage find/submit require only a found employee and positive kilometres. Status, leave date, grade and car ownership are not checked; leavers can submit claims too.
rules.note: Only the request wizard checks isActive(); counterpart of MF-R04.

navigation_questions.business_question: What are the company-car rules for Germany?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Always the single DE row; no effective dating, so rule changes apply retroactively.

navigation_questions.navigation: select e from Employee e where lower(employeeNo|lastName|firstName) like %t% order by lastName, firstName (max 50)
navigation_questions.business_question: Which employees match this name or number fragment?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Includes leavers (status T); alphabetical; truncated at 50 with no indication.

navigation_questions.navigation: select e from Employee e where e.employeeNo = :n
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Exact match; wizard and mileage Suchen trim+upper-case first, statement/assignment/mileage URL param do not.

navigation_questions.navigation: select a from Assignment a join fetch a.vehicle where a.employee = :e order by a.startDate desc
navigation_questions.business_question: Which cars has this employee had, newest first?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Includes returned and open assignments; no date filter (statement filters overlap in Java).

navigation_questions.navigation: currentAssignment(e): first a in assignments(e) with endDate null
navigation_questions.business_question: Does this employee currently have a company car, and which?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Stops at the first open one by latest start; if data had two open, the older is hidden.

navigation_questions.navigation: select v from Vehicle v where v.owner is null and not exists (open Assignment for v) order by v.plate
navigation_questions.business_question: Which pool cars are free to hand out?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Requires both no owner and no open assignment; sorted by plate; snapshot at step 1.

navigation_questions.navigation: select v from Vehicle v where v.plate = :p
navigation_questions.business_question: Which car has this number plate?

navigation_questions.navigation: select a from Assignment a join fetch a.employee where a.vehicle = :v and a.endDate is null
navigation_questions.business_question: Who currently has this car and since when?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Takes the first open assignment if several (no ordering); none means the car is in the pool.

navigation_questions.navigation: select c from MileageClaim c where c.employee = :e and c.claimDate between :f and :t order by c.claimDate
navigation_questions.business_question: Which mileage claims did this employee make in this date range (last 6 months / the statement month)?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Oldest first, all statuses; statement then keeps only APPROVED.

navigation_questions.navigation: requestCar: em.find(Employee,id); persist/find Vehicle; v.setOwner(emp); persist CarRequest; persist Assignment
navigation_questions.business_question: Hand this car to this employee from this date.
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Links car to employee as owner and opens a new assignment; request recorded as already DELIVERED.

navigation_questions.business_question: Take this car back from its holder on this date.
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Closes the assignment (kept as history) and returns the car to the pool; nothing is deleted.

navigation_questions.business_question: What car (plate, list price) belongs to this assignment?
navigation_questions.answer_semantics: Current vehicle data, not a snapshot at assignment time.
